response: ["When melanoma is suspected, the whole lesion should be completely excised with a narrow (1-3mm) margin to perform histological diagnosis.", "Incisional biopsies can be performed on large lesions such as lesions on the face (e.g., lentigo maligna), acral lesions and on the genitalia.", "Surgical excision with histologically negative margins is the recommended and first-line treatment for primary cutaneous melanoma of any thickness, as well as for melanoma in situ.", "Surgical margins should be based on tumor thickness.", "Sentinel lymph node biopsy, when indicated, should be performed before wide excision of the primary tumor, and in the same operative setting, whenever possible.", "The criteria driving the 4-point score are pigment_network (atypical, 2 points), dots_and_globules (irregular, 1 point), and regression_structures (combinations, 1 point).", "Pigment_network is considered atypical and contributes 2 points to the score.", "Dots_and_globules are considered irregular and contribute 1 point to the score.", "Regression_structures are considered combinations and contribute 1 point to the score.", "These features are major or minor features that contribute to melanoma suspicion.", "On the image, one should look for an atypical pigment network with irregular meshes and thickened lines.", "On the image, one should look for irregularly distributed dots or globules and combinations of regression structures such as white scar-like areas and blue peppering."]
